real_takeaways: Within-workflow (variance controlled across conditions), compact won 2, tied 3, lost 1 vs raw. The two compact wins were on questions where raw REFUSED — compression made facts more reachable across long context.
Compression ratio is 30-50x (matches our production claim of '5-9x' for compact mode being conservative).
Compact LOSES when the question requires a needle detail that the compressor decided not to include (q2 lemon poppyseed). Structured compression has a recall-precision tradeoff — needles get pruned.

Long-context Q&A is intrinsically noisy at this scale (the 33% vs 83% swing). This is the same instability memory.inc, Mastra et al. are trying to solve — but our specific compression v1 only mildly helps.
honest_next_steps: DO NOT publish any number from this run. n is too small, variance too high, memory contamination corrupts compact condition.
Fix memory contamination first (explicit prompt OR alternative subagent type). Re-run small sample to confirm fix.

Then expand to 30-60 questions with random sampling once methodology is solid.
